bugs.summary: AssertExpectationsForObjects now type-asserts *Mock instead of Mock, so a mock.Mock passed by value (the deprecated AssertExpectationsForObjects(t, myMock.Mock) form, which used to work and log a deprecation warning) no longer matches that branch. It falls through to the unchecked obj.(assertExpectationser), and because AssertExpectations has a pointer receiver a Mock value does not implement the interface, so the call panics instead of checking expectations.
bugs.trigger: AssertExpectationsForObjects(t, myMock.Mock) with a value mock.Mock: before this change it logged the deprecation and checked expectations; after it, obj.(assertExpectationser) panics with 'interface conversion: mock.Mock is not mock.assertExpectationser'. The fix (#1795, issue #1227) uses a checked type assertion and reports a test error instead; its test passes Mock{} and expects one Errorf.

related_valid: Mock now holds sync.Mutex by value, so copying a Mock (passing it by value anywhere) copies the lock; go vet flags this.
The deprecation message for passing myMock.Mock is unreachable for the by-value form it describes.
